answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because tundra only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice gale is enforced by the ledger itself: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any kernel approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
